modelName: CT unwrapped-diagram and SSPz geometry reference
purpose: Visualize how angular-longitudinal candidate geometry can affect the configured slice thickness, using configured-output SSPz center-shape and low-amplitude-tail views, with the nearest-bracketing gap ratio retained only as a geometry audit.

referenceImplementation.note: The web calculation now follows only the Python application's actual-data-only 360-degree path. Its 180-degree half-scan paths are not used. The web implementation remains a focused port rather than a literal reproduction of every feature.

scanCalculationConvention: Each SSPz is calculated from one actual-data family sampled at equally spaced relative tube angles beta in the half-open interval 0 <= beta < 360 degrees. Angles from 180 to 360 degrees are calculated by the same actual-data rule as angles from 0 to 180 degrees; they are not generated by converting, copying, or relabeling a 180-degree half-scan. Within each beta, the nearest candidate with z smaller than z0 and the nearest candidate with z larger than z0 are selected over the ideal infinite helix and assigned linear interpolation weights normalized to one. Smaller/larger z refers to the longitudinal coordinate, not to the upper/lower direction of the unwrapped diagram. No fixed candidate support cutoff or scanner-specific redundancy weight is applied.
angleConvention: The diagram uses a model-relative tube angle beta with 0 degrees at the top and 360 degrees at the bottom. It is not a measured absolute tube angle. The drawn endpoint at 360 degrees closes the displayed helix period but is not double-counted in SSPz integration.
overlayConvention: The overlay samples 360 equally spaced relative reconstruction states within one table feed per rotation. All 360 configured-output profiles are rendered as 360 separate thin paths without state decimation, an overlaid pointwise summary curve, or a filled range. These are not 360 acquisitions or measured absolute tube angles. Every profile is peak-normalized and kept on its native z-minus-z0 coordinate without additional alignment. The linear center-shape view derives its symmetric horizontal domain from configured-output values at or above 10 percent of peak. The separate logarithmic tail view derives its domain from configured-output values at or above 0.1 percent. Off/on panels share a domain only within the same view role. The internal pre-thickness response is not exposed as a public SSPz or width result.
candidateDisplayConvention: The overview spans every turn containing a row-wise nearest smaller-z or larger-z candidate over the selected full-scan period plus one neighboring turn on either side, and renders every detector row without row subsampling. Detector-row identity is encoded by hue. All 0-to-360-degree actual-data trajectories use solid lines; no opposing-data family is synthesized. The off/on panels share a horizontal scale. The ideal helix is infinite; the displayed finite range is a reproducible view around the target plane, not the complete acquisition trajectory.
weightDisplayConvention: Candidate markers have a fixed size. Within each detector-row hue, color intensity from pale to dark represents the normalized linear interpolation weight from low to high. All markers are circles because the full-scan calculation contains one actual-data family.
geometryIndicatorConvention: For every relative reconstruction state and tube angle, delta-z is the distance between the nearest candidates bracketing the target plane; an exact candidate match is assigned delta-z zero because no interpolation is required. Delta-z divided by configured slice thickness T is displayed on a shared linear color scale. It is an acquisition-geometry sensitivity indicator, not a reconstruction success criterion or a prediction of a proprietary scanner SSPz.
